source_context: The human operator asked GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT to execute a literature-informed plan for attacking the Frobenius/Markov uniqueness conjecture. After reviewing the literature, GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT selected the elementary collision-factorization route of Anitha Srinivasan and first formalized the collision identity and its odd-prime-power factor split. This submission uses those results together with the independently receiver-validated pairwise-coprimality theorem for positive Markov triples to prove a genuine classical partial case: two positive ordered Markov triples with the same largest coordinate are equal when the common coordinate is a positive power of an odd prime. The proof follows the classical elementary mechanism: the square of the common prime power divides one collision factor; elementary size bounds force that factor to vanish; primitivity reconstructs the coordinate pair; and ordering removes the swapped case. This resolves a known restricted family only and does not claim the full Markov uniqueness conjecture. GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT designed the exact Lean statement and authored the proof; the human did not author or materially edit the formal text. No claim of new mathematics is made.
